title: Unifying Performance and Equity via Percentile Optimization and Cell-Free Massive MIMO
authors: Ahmad Khan, Hussein A. Ammar, Raviraj Adve
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33982v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Improving the throughput of the weakest users is a central objective of wireless resource allocation, and the objective around which the user-centric cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (UC-mMIMO) architecture is built. This paper brings the two together by formulating and solving percentile programs for UC-mMIMO networks. We maximize the sum-least-qth-percentile (SLqP) rate via downlink power control, a utility that targets the user equipments (UEs) in the lowest q percentile of the rate distribution and subsumes max-min-rate and sum-rate maximization as special cases. The problem is non-convex, non-smooth and NP-hard. The cyclic maximization approach of one of the previous percentile optimization series does not carry over: the coherent joint transmission technique introduces cross terms in the powers that destroy the block-concavity on which it relies. We develop a change of variables that restores block-concavity, yielding an algorithm with closed-form auxiliary updates and a concave power update, and we give a self-contained proof of non-decreasing convergence to a directional stationary point. Simulations establish two facts: first, percentile optimization retains its value in an architecture with no cell edges; relative to the weighted minimum mean-square error benchmark, it raises the average rate of the lowest-10th-percentile UEs by 56--72% and Jain's fairness index from below 0.92 to above 0.99. Second, compared directly with massive MIMO and small cells under the same SLqP utility, UC-mMIMO delivers the highest lower-percentile rates at every access point density tested, by up to 62% and 2.7$\times$ respectively, at the same fairness, and its advantage widens with densification.

title: The Golomb--Welch conjecture for lattice tilings
authors: Bocong Chen, Jing Huang, Gaojun Luo
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33983v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove the Golomb--Welch conjecture for lattice tilings: for every $n\ge3$ and $r\ge2$, the integer lattice $\Z^n$ admits no lattice tiling by Lee balls $B_n(r)$ of radius $r$. Together with the classical constructions for $n\le2$ and for $r=1$, this determines all parameters for which a lattice Lee tiling exists. Equivalently, we show that every abelian Cayley graph of even degree $2n\ge6$ and diameter $r\ge2$ has strictly fewer than $|B_n(r)|$ vertices.

title: A class of Niho type four-valued cross-correlation functions between sequences of different periods
authors: Yao Yao, Yufei Wang, Yongbo Xia, Nian Li, Xiangyong Zeng
abstract:
arXiv:2610.34010v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Determining the cross-correlation distributions between $m$-sequences and their decimated sequences is an important problem in sequence design. For two positive integers $n$ and $k$ with $n=2k$, this paper investigates the cross-correlation function between a binary $m$-sequence $\{u(t)\}$ of period $2^{n}-1$ and its $2^{\gcd(s,k)}+1$ short-period decimated sequences $\{u(dt+l)\}$, where the decimation $d=\frac{2^s}{2^s+1}(2^k-1)+1$ satisfies $1<s>v_2(k)$. The cross-correlation function is proved to be four-valued and its value distribution is completely determined. Several previously known binary cross-correlation functions are included in our result as special cases.

title: MDS codes containing a fixed subcode over finite field extensions
authors: Yangcheng Li, Pingzhi Yuan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.34016v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $2\le k\le n$ and let $U\le\mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a fixed $(k-1)$-dimensional linear code. We study the $[n,k]$ maximum distance separable (MDS) codes over finite extensions of $\mathbb{F}_q$ that contain the scalar extension of $U$. Our approach constructs an auxiliary linear code from \(U\). Its full-weight words characterize the desired MDS completions. We prove that \(U\) admits an \([n,k]\) MDS completion over some finite extension of \(\mathbb{F}_q\) if and only if \(d(U)\ge n-k+1\). When this condition holds, the number of these MDS codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$ is \[\#\left\{W\le\mathbb{F}_{q^m}^n:U\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^m}\subseteq W,\ \dim_{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}} W=k,\ W\text{ is MDS}\right\}=\frac{\chi_{\delta_GM(G)}(q^m)}{q^m-1},\] where $G$ is a generator matrix of $U$, $\delta_GM(G)$ is its represented derived matroid, and $\chi_{\delta_GM(G)}$ is its characteristic polynomial. In particular, the formula determines existence over each extension field and the least extension degree for which such an MDS code exists. Examples show that these counts may distinguish different representations of the same column matroid, while monomially inequivalent codes may have identical counts over every finite extension.

title: Back to Basics: Formal Analysis Hints Improve Weak-to-Strong Monitoring
authors: Daniel Ben-Levi, Judah Goldfeder, Mateusz Dziemian, Raja Moreno
abstract:
arXiv:2610.34064v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frontier agentic systems are capable of taking misaligned actions that may cause significant harm. Monitoring techniques are developed to oversee these systems in order to detect and prevent dangerous actions. However, current state-of-the-art monitors suffer from four persistent failure modes: complete detection failures, partial detections, accepting false benign framings, and suspicion score calibration errors. These failure cases can be efficiently combated by augmenting transcripts with supplementary hints, spanning command provenance, security-sensitive action flags, and task-disallowed effect markers. Provenance links allow for the recognition of diffuse attacks, while security and authorization flags simultaneously enable subtle attack recognition and provide an explicit reason for monitors to doubt the false benign framings they encounter, reducing rationalization and improving calibration. We find that augmenting weak extract-and-evaluate monitors with these hints significantly boosts performance with minimal computational cost. Furthermore, a failure mode analysis confirms that hints can remediate all four failure modes, notably almost entirely eliminating detection failures. A series of ablation studies emphasizes the efficiency and potential of the augmented extract-and-evaluate approach. Synthesizing our findings, we propose a tractable two-pronged approach toward enabling weak-to-strong monitoring.
